claims.text: Net sales decreased $746.2 million, or 13.6%, to $4,722.1 million in 2023, with a 13.5% comparable-sales decline, an operating loss of $387.4 million, and diluted loss per share of ($16.53). Long-term debt rose to $406.3 million, available liquidity under the 2022 Credit Agreement fell from $376.9M to $281.3M, and management took $148.6M of non-cash store impairments plus a $146M deferred-tax valuation allowance.

claims.text: Big Lots operated 1,392 stores in 48 states at fiscal 2023 year-end (Feb 3, 2024), down 33 from 1,425 in 2022. Plans for 2024 include opening ~3 new stores and closing a number of stores. 172 store leases expire in 2024 of which 141 have renewal options. Real estate team has identified more than 500 markets for future growth.

claims.text: Big Lots reports Broyhill-branded sales fell to ~8.3% of total sales in 2023 (from ~12.4% in 2022) due to closure of largest Broyhill supplier in Q4 2022; supply was restored in H2 2023 with new vendors. The retailer also reports partnerships with Instacart, Shipt, DoorDash and Uber Eats for fulfillment, plus a private-label credit card via a third party. These are claimed material brand and partnership relationships.

claims.text: On April 18, 2024 BIG entered the First Amendment to its 2022 Credit Agreement that permitted a new Term Loan Facility, expanded the collateral package to include non-working-capital assets and a mortgage on corporate HQ in Columbus OH, added a Term Pushdown Reserve to the borrowing base, increased interest-rate spreads, and replaced the fixed-charge coverage covenant with an Excess Availability Covenant. The simultaneous addition of a Term Loan, additional collateral and covenant restructuring is a hallmark distress sign.

claims.text: Project Springboard is a cost-reduction/productivity initiative launched in 2023 targeting >$200M operating-income improvement (40% from reduced COGS, 40% from other GM, 20% from SG&A). Management says they are 'confident' significant savings will be realized in 2024 and beyond. This is an explicit announced (planned) cost-savings target subject to Calibration Heuristic 3 — needs M-side check vs operating results.

claims.text: Forward guidance: management explicitly states 'We expect to return to comp sales growth in 2024 and to significantly improve our gross margin in 2024 compared to 2023.' After a 13.5% comp decline in 2023 this is a sharp forward inflection claim with no specified driver beyond Project Springboard and Operation North Star milestones.
